meta.name: Cluster protein intensities (highly multiplexed imaging)
meta.description: Clustering path for per-cell protein intensities from highly multiplexed imaging (imaging mass cytometry, CyCIF, CODEX): z-score each marker, then PCA → neighbors → Leiden → UMAP (2D, plus a 3-component UMAP in obsm['X_umap_3d']). Deliberately omits normalize_total/log1p and highly-variable-gene selection, which assume transcript counts.
meta.provenance: Follows the marker-scaling-then-Leiden phenotyping path of the Bodenmiller group's IMC data-analysis book (https://bodenmillergroup.github.io/IMCDataAnalysis/), expressed with scanpy's scale/PCA/neighbors and graspologic (MIT) Leiden.

readme: For panels measuring **protein intensity per cell**, not transcript counts — the tables that `io.steinbock` and `io.mcmicro` produce. Library-size normalization and log1p exist to tame count depth and are wrong here: the matrix is already a mean intensity per cell per channel, and a 40-marker panel has no uninformative genes to select away. Instead each marker is z-scored across cells (`sc.pp.scale`, clipped at `max_value` so one saturated cell cannot dominate a component), which puts dim and bright channels on comparable footing, and the standard PCA → neighbors → Leiden path follows. Clusters land in `obs[cluster_key]` and are cell phenotypes rather than transcriptional states. Follow with 'Neighborhood analysis (cellular neighborhoods)' to find the tissue niches those phenotypes form.

params.name: max_value
params.tooltip: clip z-scores above this, so a saturated cell cannot dominate a component

params.name: cluster_key
params.tooltip: obs column to write the cell-phenotype cluster labels into

params.name: resolution
params.tooltip: Leiden resolution: higher = more, smaller clusters
